Porcelain Tiles for Bathroom
The bathroom is a sanctuary within the home, a place for relaxation, rejuvenation, and personal care. Choosing the right flooring and wall materials is crucial for creating a functional and aesthetically pleasing bathroom environment. Porcelain tiles offer a myriad of benefits that make them an excellent choice for bathrooms. In this article, we'll delve into the advantages of porcelain tiles for bathrooms, design tips, and practical considerations to help you transform your bathroom into a stylish and functional space.
Benefits of Porcelain Tiles for Bathrooms
Water Resistance: Porcelain tiles are inherently water-resistant, making them ideal for humid and moisture-prone areas like bathrooms. They are impervious to water penetration, preventing damage and mold growth.
Durability: Porcelain tiles are durable and long-lasting, able to withstand heavy foot traffic, impact, and wear. They are also resistant to scratches, stains, and chemical damage, ensuring a low-maintenance surface.
Versatility: Available in a wide range of colors, patterns, sizes, and finishes, porcelain tiles offer endless design possibilities for bathroom floors, walls, shower enclosures, and backsplashes.
Easy Maintenance: Porcelain tiles are easy to clean and maintain, requiring simple sweeping, mopping, or occasional scrubbing with a mild detergent to keep them looking pristine.
Hygienic: Non-porous and hypoallergenic, porcelain tiles inhibit the growth of bacteria, fungi, and allergens, promoting a healthier bathroom environment.
Design Tips for Using Porcelain Tiles for Bathroom
Color Palette: Choose light and neutral colors for a spacious and airy feel in small bathrooms. Darker tones can add drama and contrast, especially in larger bathrooms with ample natural light.
Tile Size: Consider using large format tiles to create a seamless and visually expansive look. Subway tiles, mosaic patterns, and geometric designs are also popular choices for adding texture and interest.
Accent Tiles: Use accent tiles or decorative inserts to create focal points, borders, or feature walls in shower areas, above vanities, or around mirrors. Mix and match patterns for a personalized touch.
Flooring Versatility: Opt for slip-resistant porcelain tiles for bathroom floors to enhance safety, especially in wet areas like shower floors. Textured finishes or matte surfaces offer better traction.
Wet Room Design: For a modern and sleek look, consider a wet room design with floor-to-ceiling porcelain tiles, minimalistic fixtures, and a barrier-free shower area for a seamless transition.
Practical Considerations and Installation Tips
Subfloor Preparation: Ensure the subfloor is clean, level, and properly waterproofed before tile installation to prevent water damage and ensure a stable base.
Grout Selection: Choose grout colors that complement your tile design and enhance the overall aesthetic of your bathroom. Seal grout lines regularly to maintain cleanliness and prevent discoloration.
Underfloor Heating: Porcelain tiles are compatible with underfloor heating systems, providing warmth and comfort underfoot during colder months.
Shower Enclosures: Use waterproof membranes and proper tile adhesives for shower enclosures to ensure water-tight seals and prevent moisture infiltration.

Porcelain Tiles vs. Other Flooring Options: A Comparison Guide
Porcelain Tiles vs. Other Flooring Options: A Comparison Guide Introduction: Choosing the right flooring option for your home or business is a significant decision. With various materials available, it's essential to understand the pros and cons of each. In this blog, we will compare porcelain tiles with other popular flooring options. It's allowing you to make an informed choice that meets your specific needs.
Durability and Longevity: Porcelain tiles are renowned for their durability and longevity. They are incredibly resistant to scratches, stains, and wear, making them ideal for high-traffic areas. In comparison, materials like laminate or vinyl may not offer the same level of durability. Making porcelain tiles a more reliable choice in the long run.
Aesthetics and Design Options: Porcelain tiles come in a wide array of designs, patterns, and colors, allowing you to achieve the desired look for your space. Whether you prefer a modern, classic, or rustic aesthetic, porcelain tiles can cater to your specific style. In contrast, other flooring options like carpet or vinyl may have limited design choices, restricting your ability to customize the look of your space.
Maintenance and Cleaning: Porcelain tiles are relatively low maintenance. They are resistant to stains, and any spills or messes can be easily wiped away. Regular sweeping and occasional mopping is typically sufficient to keep them looking clean and fresh. On the other hand, carpet requires regular vacuuming and professional cleaning, while hardwood floors need periodic refinishing and polishing.
Moisture Resistance: One of the significant advantages of porcelain tiles is their excellent moisture resistance. They are impervious to water, making them suitable for areas prone to spills or humidity, such as kitchens, bathrooms, or basements. In comparison, materials like hardwood or laminate can be adversely affected by moisture, leading to warping or mold growth.
Allergies and Indoor Air Quality: For individuals with allergies or respiratory sensitivities, porcelain tiles are a great choice. Unlike carpet, which can trap allergens such as dust mites, pet dander, or pollen, porcelain tiles have a smooth and non-porous surface that does not harbor allergens. This helps improve indoor air quality and creates a healthier living environment.
Eco-Friendliness: If sustainability is a priority, porcelain tiles are an eco-friendly flooring option. They are making from natural materials, such as clay, and do not release harmful VOCs (volatile organic compounds) into the air. In comparison, some laminate or vinyl flooring options may contain chemicals that can impact indoor air quality.
Comfort and Underfoot Feel: While porcelain tiles offer exceptional durability, they may not provide the same level of cushioning or underfoot comfort as materials like carpet or cork. If you prioritize a softer and more comfortable feel underfoot, alternative flooring options may be more suitable for areas where you spend a lot of time standing or walking.
Cost Considerations: Porcelain tiles can vary in price depending on factors such as the quality, design, and installation complexity. While they may have a higher upfront cost compared to materials like vinyl or carpet. Their longevity and durability often make them a cost-effective choice in the long term. It's important to weigh the initial investment against the lifespan and maintenance requirements of different flooring options.
Installation and DIY Potential: The installation process for porcelain tiles can be more complex compared to some other flooring options. Achieving a professional finish often requires the expertise of a skilled installer. In contrast, materials like laminate or vinyl often come with simple installation systems, making them more DIY-friendly.
Sound Insulation: If sound insulation is a priority, carpet or cork flooring options tend to provide better acoustic properties compared to porcelain tiles. Porcelain tiles can transmit sound more effectively. Which may result in increased noise levels in multi-story buildings or rooms with high sound activity.
Conclusion:
When comparing flooring options. It's essential to consider factors such as durability, aesthetics, maintenance, moisture resistance, allergies, eco-friendliness, comfort, cost, installation complexity, and sound insulation. Porcelain tiles offer a compelling combination of these factors. Making them a versatile and practical choice for many residential and commercial spaces. Assess your specific requirements and preferences to determine which flooring option aligns best with your needs. And enhances the overall look and functionality of your space. What is Porcelain Tile?
Porcelain tiles have become an increasingly popular choice in the world of interior design and construction, thanks to their exceptional durability, versatility, and timeless aesthetic appeal. As a leading porcelain tile company in the UK, it’s important for us to help our customers understand the unique qualities that make porcelain tiles such a smart and stylish option.
Porcelain tile is a type of ceramic tile made from finely ground clay minerals such as kaolinite, combined with other materials including feldspar, quartz, and carefully selected pigments. These raw materials are blended into a homogeneous mixture, which is then shaped into tiles through processes like extrusion or pressing.
What truly sets porcelain tiles apart is their high-temperature firing process — typically over 2100°F (1150°C). This intense heat transforms the clay and minerals into a vitrified, glass-like material, giving the tiles their renowned strength, density, and resistance to wear.
Why Choose Porcelain Tile?
One of the standout benefits of porcelain tile is its impressive durability. Thanks to its dense structure and rigorous firing process, it’s highly resistant to cracks, scratches, and general wear and tear — making it perfect for use in homes, offices, and high-traffic areas.
Porcelain tiles also absorb far less water than standard ceramic tiles due to their low porosity. This makes them highly resistant to stains, moisture, and frost, making them ideal for both indoor and outdoor use in a variety of settings.

Are Porcelain Tiles Suitable for Both Residential and Commercial?
When it comes to choosing flooring materials for your residential or commercial space, one option that often stands out is porcelain tiles. Porcelain Known for their durability, versatility, and aesthetic appeal, porcelain tiles have gained popularity in both residential and commercial settings. In this blog post, we will explore whether porcelain tiles are suitable for both residential and commercial use, examining their characteristics, benefits, and considerations for each environment.
Understanding Porcelain Tiles:
Porcelain tiles are made from a dense, fine-grained ceramic material fired at high temperatures. This manufacturing process results in a tile that is highly resistant to water, stains, and scratches. Porcelain tiles come in various finishes, including polished, unpolished, textured, and glazed, offering a wide range of options to suit different design preferences.
Benefits of Porcelain Tiles:
a) Durability: Porcelain tiles are incredibly durable and can withstand heavy foot traffic. It makes them suitable for both residential and commercial areas.
b) Water and Stain Resistance: The non-porous nature of porcelain tiles makes them resistant to water absorption and stains, making them ideal for areas prone to moisture, spills, and high traffic.
c) Low Maintenance: Porcelain tiles are relatively easy to clean and require minimal maintenance. Making them convenient for both residential and commercial spaces.
d) Aesthetic Appeal: With a wide variety of colors, patterns, and textures available. Porcelain tiles can enhance the visual appeal of any space, whether residential or commercial.
Residential Applications:
a) Flooring: Porcelain tiles are an excellent choice for residential flooring, including entryways, kitchens, bathrooms, and living areas. Their durability and resistance to moisture make them suitable for high-traffic areas and spaces exposed to water.
b) Wall Tiles: Porcelain tiles are using as wall tiles in bathrooms and kitchens, adding a touch of elegance and providing a practical solution for areas prone to splashes and spills.
Commercial Applications:
a) Retail Spaces: Porcelain tiles can withstand the demands of retail environments, including shopping malls, boutiques, and showrooms, where foot traffic is high. They can also create an inviting and visually appealing atmosphere.
b) Hospitality Sector: Hotels, restaurants, and cafes can benefit from the durability and low maintenance requirements of porcelain tiles. They offer an ideal flooring solution that can withstand heavy use while maintaining a polished look.
c) Offices and Public Spaces: Porcelain tiles are well-suited for office buildings, airports, and other public spaces due to their durability, resistance to wear and tear, and ease of maintenance.
Conclusion:
Porcelain tiles can be used for both residential and commercial use. Thanks to their exceptional durability, water resistance, low maintenance requirements, and aesthetic appeal. Whether you are looking to enhance your home's interior or create a stylish and functional commercial space, porcelain tiles offer a versatile and reliable solution. Consider your specific requirements, such as foot traffic, moisture levels, and design preferences, when choosing porcelain tiles for your project. How is porcelain tile different from ceramic tile?
As a leading provider of premium tiles in the UK, Surfaces Tiles aims to provide our customers with comprehensive knowledge about different types of tiles. This blog post will delve into the fascinating world of porcelain tiles and ceramic tiles, highlighting their differences and helping you make informed decisions for your next tile project. Whether you're considering wall tiles, floor tiles, kitchen tiles, bathroom tiles, or outdoor tiles, understanding the disparities between porcelain and ceramic tiles is essential. Read on to discover the unique characteristics and benefits of porcelain tiles and how they set themselves apart from their ceramic counterparts.
Composition and Manufacturing Process:
Porcelain Tiles: Porcelain tiles are made from a special type of clay. Known for their high density and low porosity. This clay is fired at extremely high temperatures. Resulting in a dense, durable, and moisture-resistant tile. The manufacturing process involves compressing the clay under intense pressure, ensuring the final product is exceptionally strong.
Ceramic Tiles: Ceramic tiles are made from a mixture of clay, minerals, and water. Compared to porcelain tiles, these tiles require less heat when being fired. Resulting in a more porous and less dense structure. This makes ceramic tiles better suited for indoor applications with lower foot traffic.
Durability and Strength:
Porcelain Tiles: Porcelain tiles are famous for their exceptional durability. The high firing temperatures make them extremely strong, and resistant to scratches, stains, and fading. Their dense structure enables them to withstand heavy foot traffic, making them ideal for high-traffic areas such as commercial spaces or busy households.
Ceramic Tiles: While ceramic tiles are durable, they are generally not as strong as porcelain tiles. They are more susceptible to chipping and cracking under significant pressure. Consequently, ceramic tiles are more commonly used for residential spaces with lighter foot traffic.
Water Absorption:
Porcelain Tiles: Porcelain tiles have an incredibly low water absorption rate, typically less than 0.5%. This property makes them highly resistant to water damage, making them suitable for areas exposed to moisture, such as bathrooms, kitchens, and outdoor spaces. Porcelain tiles are also less prone to freeze-thaw damage, making them an excellent choice for outdoor applications in colder climates.
Ceramic Tiles: Ceramic tiles have a higher water absorption rate, usually around 3% to 7%. While they are still suitable for most indoor applications, they may not be the best choice for areas with high humidity or direct water exposure.
Design Options:
Porcelain Tiles: Porcelain tiles offer a wide range of design options, including various colors, patterns, and textures. Modern manufacturing techniques can even mimic the appearance of natural materials like stone or wood, providing versatile options for both classic and contemporary designs.
Ceramic Tiles: Similar to porcelain tiles, ceramic tiles come in a variety of designs. However, the options may be more limited when compared to porcelain. Ceramic tiles are available in an array of colors and patterns, offering ample opportunities to personalize your space.
The differences between porcelain tiles and ceramic tiles lie in their composition, durability, water absorption, and design options. While both types of tiles have their merits, porcelain tiles, with their superior strength, low water absorption, and wide range of design choices, are often the preferred choice for high-traffic areas, bathrooms, kitchens, and outdoor applications.

What are the main types of tiles?
What are the main types of tiles? Tiles can be categorized into various types based on their material, design, and purpose. Here are some of the main types of tiles:
Ceramic Tiles: Manufacturers make these tiles from clay and fire them at high temperatures. They have gained popularity due to their durability and water resistance. Ceramic tiles come in various colors, sizes, and finishes.
Porcelain Tiles: These tiles, made from clay, undergo firing at higher temperatures, resulting in higher density and durability compared to ceramic tiles. People appreciate their excellent resistance to water, stains, and scratches, making them suitable for both indoor and outdoor use.
Glass Tiles: Manufacturers produce these tiles using glass, offering a wide range of colors, sizes, and finishes. People find glass tiles appealing due to their reflective and translucent properties, adding a unique and modern touch to any space. They often use glass tiles as accents or decorative elements.
Natural Stone Tiles: Manufacturers create natural stone tiles using various types of stone, such as marble, granite, slate, limestone, and travertine. These tiles provide a luxurious and elegant look, featuring unique patterns and textures. Users need to regularly seal and maintain natural stone tiles.
Mosaic Tiles: These small tiles, usually made from ceramic, glass, or natural stone, form intricate patterns or designs. They serve as decorative accents, backsplashes, or feature walls.
Quarry Tiles: Manufacturers produce quarry tiles from unglazed clay, giving them a reddish-brown color. People choose these tiles for their durability, commonly using them in high-traffic areas like kitchens, hallways, and outdoor spaces.
Vinyl Tiles: Vinyl tiles are synthetic tiles made from PVC (polyvinyl chloride) and other additives. They come in a wide variety of colors, designs, and textures. Vinyl tiles gained popularity due to their affordability, durability, and ease of installation.
Cement Tiles: Manufacturers handcraft cement tiles, also known as encaustic tiles, using a mixture of cement, sand, and pigments. These tiles are known for their vibrant colors, intricate patterns, and durability. People often use cement tiles to create decorative floors or backsplashes.
Metal Tiles: Manufacturers make metal tiles from materials such as stainless steel, aluminum, copper, or brass. People appreciate their sleek and contemporary appearance, commonly using them as accents or backsplashes in modern designs.
These are just a few examples of the main types of tiles available. Each type has its own characteristics, advantages, and considerations, so it's important to choose the one that best suits your specific needs and preferences. How to Clean and Maintain Your Porcelain Tiles for Long-Lasting Beauty
As a proud owner of porcelain tiles, you know that they bring elegance and durability to your home. To keep them looking their best and to preserve their pristine beauty for years to come, proper cleaning and maintenance are essential. In this blog, we'll guide you How to Clean and Maintain Your Porcelain Tiles and offer valuable tips to ensure they stand the test of time.
1. Understanding Porcelain Tiles
Before diving into cleaning and maintenance, let's take a moment to understand what porcelain tiles are. Porcelain tiles are made from finely ground clay and other natural materials, kiln-fired at high temperatures, making them incredibly dense and water-resistant. These qualities make them ideal for high-traffic areas like kitchens and bathrooms.
2. Regular Sweeping and Dusting
One of the simplest yet most effective ways to maintain your porcelain tiles is through regular sweeping and dusting. Dust, dirt, and debris can accumulate on the surface, leading to potential scratching. Using a soft broom or a microfiber dust mop, sweep the floor regularly to keep it clean and prevent any abrasive particles from damaging the tiles.
3. Mopping with Warm Water
For routine cleaning, warm water alone can do wonders. Avoid using harsh chemicals as they might strip away the protective glaze on the tiles. Instead, dampen a mop or cloth with warm water and gently clean the porcelain surface. Dry the area thoroughly afterward to prevent water spots.
4. Addressing Spills and Stains Promptly
Accidents happen, and spills are inevitable. When a spill occurs, it's crucial to act quickly to prevent staining. Use a soft cloth or paper towel to blot the spill gently. Avoid rubbing the stain, as it can spread and become more difficult to remove. If needed, you can use a mild pH-balanced cleaner specifically formulated for porcelain tiles.
5. Dealing with Tough Stains
Some stains may be more stubborn and require a bit more effort to remove. For such stains, consider creating a paste with baking soda and water. Apply the paste to the stain, let it sit for a few minutes, and then scrub gently with a soft brush. Rinse the area thoroughly with warm water and wipe it dry.
6. Avoiding Abrasive Cleaners and Tools
As much as you may be tempted to use abrasive cleaners or harsh scrubbing tools, resist the urge! Abrasive cleaners and scrub brushes can scratch the glaze and damage the tiles' surface. Stick to soft cloths, microfiber mops, and non-abrasive cleaning solutions to protect your porcelain tiles.
7. Using Mats and Rugs
Prevention is key when it comes to maintaining your porcelain tiles. Placing mats or rugs at entryways can help trap dirt and grit from shoes, reducing the amount of debris that makes its way onto the tiles. Be sure to use mats with non-slip backings to prevent any accidents.
8. Being Cautious with Heavy Furniture
While porcelain tiles are incredibly durable, heavy furniture can still cause damage, especially if it is dragged across the floor. To protect your tiles, place felt pads under the legs of furniture to prevent scratching when moving them.
9. Regular Grout Maintenance
Don't forget about the grout lines! Regularly inspect the grout for any signs of wear, cracking, or discoloration. Clean the grout lines with a mild grout cleaner or a mixture of baking soda and water. Sealing the grout every year can also help maintain its appearance and prevent stains.
10. Seasonal Deep Cleaning
Every few months, consider giving your porcelain tiles a thorough deep cleaning. Use a pH-balanced, non-abrasive cleaner designed for porcelain tiles and follow the manufacturer's instructions. This deep clean will remove any hidden dirt or grime, leaving your tiles looking fresh and beautiful.
11. Professional Cleaning and Inspection
If you have stubborn stains or are uncertain about the best cleaning methods for your tiles, it's always a good idea to consult with a professional tile cleaner. They can provide expert advice and ensure your porcelain tiles receive the best care possible.
By following these maintenance tips, your wall tiles, floor tiles, kitchen tiles, bathroom tiles, & outdoor tiles will retain their beauty and durability, adding value and charm to your home for many years to come. Proper cleaning and care will not only keep your tiles looking fantastic but will also protect your investment, making them a worthy addition to any UK home. How the USA–Iran Conflict Is Affecting the Tile Industry – Our View from Surfaces Tiles
Post Date

Post by SANTVAN PANCHAL
0 Comments
Global events often have a direct impact on the construction industry, and the ongoing conflict between the USA and Iran is no exception. The disruption around the Strait of Hormuz has created uncertainty in global shipping, increased energy costs, and affected manufacturers around the world.
At Surfaces Tiles, we import porcelain tiles primarily from Spain and India. With offices in both countries, we are in regular contact with manufacturers, shipping companies and industry partners, allowing us to closely monitor market conditions and understand how these events are affecting the tile industry.
One of the biggest challenges has been the sharp increase in natural gas prices. Gas is one of the most important components in the production of porcelain tiles, as it is used to fire the tiles at extremely high temperatures. Reports from our manufacturing partners indicate that gas prices increased by around 80% in India and 20% in Spain, putting significant pressure on production costs.
The Indian tile industry was forced to suspend production for approximately one month during April 2027 due to gas shortages and rising costs. Production has now resumed, although manufacturers are operating with revised pricing to reflect the higher manufacturing expenses.
Shipping has also been affected. Based on discussions with shipping lines and information currently available, ocean freight rates are expected to remain above normal levels for at least the next six months. Once freight markets stabilise, we expect some reduction in overall tile costs, but this is unlikely to happen immediately.
Despite these global challenges, the UK tile market has remained relatively stable compared with many other parts of the world. Since a large proportion of tiles supplied to the UK come from Spain, price increases have been more moderate than in some other markets.
As suppliers to homeowners, builders and construction companies across the UK and Ireland, we speak with our customers every day. While building material costs have increased across almost every category, we have not seen major construction companies delaying or cancelling their tile purchases. This gives us confidence that demand within the UK market remains healthy.
At Surfaces Tiles, we have not increased our selling prices during the past year, and at present we have no plans to do so. We believe the current situation is temporary and expect costs to improve once global shipping and energy markets become more stable. Rather than passing every increase directly to our customers, we have chosen to absorb much of the additional cost within our own margins.
Our advice to homeowners and trade professionals is simple: if your project is ready to proceed, there is little reason to delay purely because of tile prices. While prices have increased, the rise has been relatively modest compared with many other construction materials. However, if the conflict continues for a prolonged period, the market could experience further cost increases.
We are currently importing a larger proportion of our products from Spain rather than India, as Spanish supply offers more competitive pricing and shorter delivery times under current market conditions. We will continue to review our sourcing strategy to ensure we provide the best possible value and service to our customers.
Global markets can change quickly, and we will continue to monitor developments closely. With our teams based in both India and Spain, we are well positioned to understand changes in manufacturing, shipping and supply chains, and we will continue sharing updates as the situation evolves.
Thank you for trusting Surfaces Tiles. We remain committed to offering quality porcelain tiles at competitive prices while helping our customers make informed decisions during uncertain times.

Nowadays the tiles market is moving towards big size tiles, whether you talk about wall or floor people wants to use bigger sizes and tile shops are also promoting them due to wider availability and comfort in deliveries. The most running size for the bathroom in today’s time is 60 x 120 cm porcelain tiles. When this size was introduced, it was widely used in floor applications only but now it is widely used in bathrooms compare to floors.
While it is the most running size in the market there are many advantages you can see while purchasing this size. Like you can find many design options and colour options in this size, many finish options, many surface options etc. And along with all these advantages the major thing is that they are cheaper then compared to any other sizes available in the market. 60x120 cm porcelain tiles acquire almost 50% of the overall tile market in all the countries.
So, let’s see you want to use this tile, but you are worried that whether this tile look good in your bathroom or not because of the smaller size of the bathroom. Sometimes your tiler also suggests you go for the smaller size tiles because the bathroom size is not suitable for the bigger size.
Let me provide you some ideas where you can use this bigger size tile in your smaller size bathrooms with confidence. First, you must select the right colour of the tile when you want to use 60x120 cm size in smaller size bathrooms which are not bigger then 4x6 feet. Always select light colours like light beige, light grey, white with less visible marble figures, soft earthy colour tones or even you can try soft pastel colours.
The second thing to keep in mind is never mix two colours in your bathroom. It will make the bathroom space busier and eventually it will look smaller in size. Instead of that use the same colour highlighter with punch effect on it. If possible, use the liner punch at the level of your eyesight, approximately at the height of 4 to 6 feet from the floor.  With this combination you can also select the 60x60 cm tiles if your space is not allowing you to use the 60x120 cm tiles.
The second option is to use some vibrant and dark colours with very small-size tiles, often called subway tiles. I know I am contradicting my previous statement that use light and soft colour in the smaller size bathrooms. But here I am suggesting darker shades with a major change in the size of the tile when you are using dark colours like black, dark grey, deep blue or bottle green colour for your bathroom. Keep the finish of the tile matt of soft matt and do not use glossy tile in subway sizes as well. Glossy finish is more popular in subway tiles, but we suggest them only for the kitchen application and not for the bathroom application.
Lastly, the bathroom Accessories place a major role in smaller size bathrooms. These are the things which will provide the luxurious look to your bathroom. Try to use the slightly contrast bathroom accessories from your tiles and do not select glossy finish in the bathroom accessories as well. Try to use the matt finish accessories. Always use the LED mirrors with back lighting. It will give a proper look to your bathroom.
